scenario_meta.world_name: RPG Guild Main Character At-Will LongLive Test
scenario_meta.description: A Japanese fantasy RPG guild with 100 regular members and three always-active protagonists. This run removes predefined video task routes and forces protagonist activities to use freeform model-selected LongLive cinematic interactions.
scenario_meta.simulation_objective: Run 103 agents for 25 rounds at activation 0.15. The three protagonists activate every round and each protagonist activity must open LongLive; other activated agents may also use freeform at-will LongLive, with a 10-video-per-round cap. No predefined video task routes are available.

conditions: Still images remain allowed only for ordinary image routes such as treasure discovery.
Do not substitute images for protagonist LongLive routes in this at-will cinematic run.
image_generation.prompt_policy: Japanese fantasy RPG object or scene illustration, polished anime concept art, clear subject, no visible text, no watermark.
image_generation.default_prompt_template: {domain_label}. Create one polished still image of {image_subject} for {actor_name} and {target_name}. Include their visual context only if relevant. No visible text, no watermark.

social_rules: The guild world is fixed by JSON; do not append discovered world rules.
Ordinary Move, Item, and Custom actions are preferred before cinematic video actions.
Trade actions use explicit JSON item prices and currency inventory.
CinematicInteraction is reserved for body-cooperation interactions that ordinary JSON cannot express.
Relationship changes are judged per interaction by the API relationship_adjustment stage and written as tensor deltas.
Per-round task chains and random guild events are generated only by the JSON-selected extra_world_functions program and stored as world memory, not as discovered world rules.
The three main characters are JSON-defined protagonists and activate every round; their directives should influence routing without bypassing normal action legality.
This at-will run removes predefined video task routes; cinematic video must use the single generic model_cinematic_interaction route.
The three main characters must use LongLive for every successful activation while obeying same-room or range target legality.
Non-main characters should use ordinary JSON actions only in this run.

ordinary_routes.image_subject: a newly discovered minor guild treasure such as a glowing charm, tiny relic, or sealed reward box
ordinary_routes.image_prompt_template: {domain_label}. Create one polished still image of {image_subject} found during a routine guild interaction involving {actor_name} and {target_name}. Make the treasure visually distinct and safe to inspect, no visible text, no watermark.

cinematic_routes.story_verb: performed a freeform LongLive interaction with
cinematic_routes.selection_guidance: Mandatory freeform at-will video route. Do not imitate the removed predefined video tasks. Invent a safe, non-sexual, context-specific two-person physical interaction from current world memory, protagonist directive, room context, and target relationship. The action must be visible in video and not expressible as a simple listed ordinary JSON route.

routing_policy.world_memory_use: Use recent_global_world_events and local_visual_state as active context. Prefer follow-up or next-phase interactions when an event/status says a prior need was already handled.
routing_policy.main_character_use: The always-active protagonists must choose context-specific freeform cinematic interactions aligned with their activity_directive and nearby feasible targets.
routing_policy.video_recommendation: Video is strongly supported up to 10 jobs per round, but every video must use the single generic model_cinematic_interaction route and invent the action from current context. There are no predefined video task options in this run.
routing_policy.forced_cinematic_policy: For force_cinematic_agent_ids, choose model_cinematic_interaction whenever video_quota_left is positive. Other activated agents may also choose model_cinematic_interaction freely when the interaction benefits from visible two-person motion; all cinematic choices must use freeform at-will action, never predefined video tasks.
routing_policy.repeat_avoidance: Avoid repeating a resolved heal/repair/rescue/coordination on the same target unless status or event memory indicates a new phase.

target_selection.main_character_note: Main characters still obey walkable map legality and approach targets through real rooms and corridors; they do not teleport or bypass blocked paths.

longlive.visual_style: Japanese fantasy RPG guild, protagonist-centered freeform body action, current story context, no predefined video task choreography, no visible text, no watermark

sprite_generation.negative_prompt: blurry, anti-aliased, soft gradients, realistic skin texture, cinematic depth of field, text, watermark, captions, title text, logo, character name, character lineup, concept sheet, reference sheet, white background, studio backdrop, floor shadow, floor reflection, cropped limbs, extra limbs, cropped head, cropped feet, boundary crossing, frame overlap, split body, detached legs, detached head

notes: Guild map display should prioritize readable structured layout from map_grid over dark generative key art.
Room-part composition should stay JSON-driven: floors, walls, props, and pickups come from a component library and room presets.
Vertex can generate isolated prop source art for component slots, but the runtime map still composes from the JSON room contract.
Idle rows are authored as four source cells for compatibility, but the runtime consumes a single stable first frame.
Walk rows remain animated and should preserve a consistent body anchor across frames.

movement.helper_text: Move the POV hero with WASD or arrow keys. Doorways defined in JSON permit room changes.

actions.label: Greet
actions.speaker_line: {self} greets {target} and opens a quick guild-side conversation.
actions.target_reply: {target} returns the greeting and settles into the room's current mood.

actions.label: Ask Focus
actions.speaker_line: {self} asks {target} what is pressing right now.

actions.label: Offer Help
actions.speaker_line: {self} offers concrete help on the next task chain.
actions.target_reply: {target} weighs the offer and points back to {room} as the immediate scene.

healing_potion.self_outcome: {self} drinks a healing potion and steadies for the next push.
healing_potion.target_outcome: {self} gives a healing potion to {target}, easing visible strain.

mana_crystal.self_outcome: {self} centers a mana crystal and sharpens magical focus.
mana_crystal.target_outcome: {self} shares a mana crystal with {target}, helping stabilize spellwork.

quest_map.self_outcome: {self} studies the quest map and reorients around the guild's next route.
quest_map.target_outcome: {self} unfolds the quest map for {target}, comparing routes and risks.

signed_commission.self_outcome: {self} rereads the signed commission and recommits to the objective.
signed_commission.target_outcome: {self} shows the signed commission to {target}, clarifying the active objective.

repair_kit.self_outcome: {self} checks the repair kit and tightens gear for the next move.
repair_kit.target_outcome: {self} uses the repair kit to help {target} tighten gear and field straps.

herb_bundle.self_outcome: {self} sorts through a herb bundle and calms down.
herb_bundle.target_outcome: {self} shares a herb bundle with {target}, softening the room's tension.

rations.self_outcome: {self} takes quick rations and keeps moving.
rations.target_outcome: {self} hands rations to {target}, buying a little breathing room.

iron_ingot.self_outcome: {self} checks the iron ingot and thinks ahead to forge work.
iron_ingot.target_outcome: {self} shows the iron ingot to {target}, turning the talk toward equipment needs.

response_templates.gift_accept: {target} accepts the offer from {self} and treats it as goodwill.
response_templates.gift_reject: {target} politely refuses the item and says it would be wasted right now.
response_templates.trade_reject: {target} refuses the deal and asks for something more relevant.
response_templates.trade_counter: {target} counters: bring {requested_item} and they will return {return_item}.
response_templates.counter_accept: {self} accepts the counteroffer and closes the trade with {target}.
response_templates.counter_reject: {self} declines the counteroffer and keeps the current loadout.

report.title: RPG Guild At-Will Main Character LongLive Story Summary
report.author: Agora Mini Interaction Runner

inventory_generation.policy: Generate compact role-appropriate actionable inventory only from the item catalog. Use property_library for non-actionable treasures, titles, clues, personal tools, debts, or keepsakes. Do not create images here; image generation is a later system step when a route requests it.

main_characters.activity_directive: Every round, actively seek, accept, advance, or close a guild quest. Prefer interactions that create concrete task progress, recruit helpers, exchange quest items, inspect maps, coordinate parties, or report results.
main_characters.private_notes: A protagonist hero who treats the guild as a living quest hub and pushes story threads forward without waiting to be invited.

main_characters.activity_directive: Every round, freely explore the guild, ask questions, observe conflicts, form opinions, discover small mysteries, and interact with whoever reveals a new part of the world.
main_characters.private_notes: A displaced noble protagonist who is not passive: she learns how the guild works by following clues, kindness, mistakes, and rumors.

main_characters.activity_directive: Every round, actively help guild members: assign resources, resolve bottlenecks, mediate disputes, support novices, connect specialists, and turn scattered events into organized guild response.
main_characters.private_notes: A protagonist guild official who keeps the building functioning and turns ordinary interactions into visible institutional support.

functions.purpose: Create or advance small parallel guild task chains every round. Use prior global events to continue, branch, or close existing threads instead of restarting them.
functions.event_policy: Prefer concrete quest-step events: new commission posted, party formed, map checked, supplies short, healer needed, forged tool ready, scouting lead returned, reward handoff due, completion celebration. Include at least one actionable next step when possible.
functions.main_character_policy: Hook the hero to quest acceptance/progress/completion, the guild cadre to coordination/resource bottlenecks, and the fallen princess to exploration or social discovery when appropriate.
functions.continuity_policy: Use titles and status_tags to show next-phase progress such as posted, recruited, equipped, departed, returned, verified, paid, archived.

functions.purpose: Generate light guild incidents that create interaction opportunities without overriding agent autonomy.
functions.event_policy: Examples are allowed as style references only: spilled potion crate, nervous rookie, damaged practice dummy, loud tavern rumor, missing quest stamp, strange mana flicker, injured familiar, misplaced reward box. The model should choose what fits the current world memory.
functions.main_character_policy: Hook protagonists only when the event naturally matches their directive; otherwise let ordinary members respond.
functions.continuity_policy: Prefer events that can be resolved or followed up through existing routes and status effects over one-off flavor.

world_progress.source: JSON extra_world_functions plus status effects and localized visual state
world_progress.routing_instruction: Treat generated task/random events as soft world memory. Route agents toward advancing, resolving, or referencing them when compatible with role, room, target legality, and current status.
status_follow_up_examples: invited_to_small_quest can lead to coordinate_party, inspect_quest_map, trade_supplies, buff_for_commission, or move_to_task rather than another identical invite.
recovered_after_training can lead to training notes, celebration, return-to-duty coordination, or ordinary chat rather than repeated healing.
gear_repaired_for_next_commission can lead to quest invite, supplies trade, or scout report rather than another repair.
